description: Cross-driver relative timer delay ceiling (2^53 ms, owned by _shared/lua/number_policy.lua MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS). Replayed by _shared/lua/test/timer_delay_ceiling_contract.lua through the macOS and Linux suites: the policy, both TimerScheduler adapters and every Linux native timer and sleep boundary.

field_semantics.milliseconds: Delay in milliseconds. The strings "inf", "-inf" and "nan" stand for the values JSON cannot spell.
field_semantics.seconds: Delay in seconds, as the TimerScheduler port receives it. Chosen so that seconds * 1000 is exact in a double and the verdict cannot depend on rounding.
field_semantics.admitted: True when the delay may reach a native timer. A finite negative delay is admitted by the ceiling policy; each caller keeps its own lower bound.

millisecond_vectors.description: The ceiling owns only the upper bound.
A year, far below the ceiling.
2^63 ms, where Lua 5.4 refuses the integer conversion and LuaJIT's is undefined.
A finite value far beyond every native range.

second_vectors.description: Fires on the next loop turn.
Finite, but infinite once converted to milliseconds.
